Medium, simplification/efficiency: [cmd/entire/cli/objectsigner.go:33](</Users/pfleidi/entire/cli/.worktrees/fix/1password-commit-signing/cmd/entire/cli/objectsigner.go:33>) and [cmd/entire/cli/objectsigner.go:129](</Users/pfleidi/entire/cli/.worktrees/fix/1password-commit-signing/cmd/entire/cli/objectsigner.go:129>) add a fresh repo open and local config parse inside the signer factory, so the new local-scope lookup runs on every checkpoint-sign attempt rather than once. Why it matters: this puts extra filesystem/git work on the signing path for every checkpoint commit. Evidence: `SignCommitBestEffort` calls `plugin.Get(plugin.ObjectSigner())` for each signing attempt in [cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/committed.go:1799](</Users/pfleidi/entire/cli/.worktrees/fix/1password-commit-signing/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/committed.go:1799>), and go-git’s plugin registry executes the registered factory on every `Get` (`.../go-git/v6/x/plugin/plugin.go:65-87`), not just the first registration. That means `git.PlainOpenWithOptions(".", DetectDotGit: true)` plus `repo.Storer.Config()` now repeat per checkpoint. Concrete fix: memoize the local-config read inside `RegisterObjectSigner` (for example with a closure-local `sync.Once`/cached `*config.Config` and cached custom-program bool), or otherwise thread an already-open repo/config into signer creation so `loadLocalConfig()` is not redoing repository discovery and config parsing on each `plugin.Get`.
